newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC wins licence in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC wins licence in Kazakhstan.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) said on Saturday that its international arm, ONGC Videsh, has become the first Indian firm to win a licence to explore for oil and gas in Kazakhstan.
ONGC said in a statement that the licence covers an area of about 10,000 square km in the former Soviet republic, which it said was a "focus area" of ONGC Videsh.

The first phase of exploratory work will involve a seismic survey estimated to cost $8 million, it said. The second phase will last three years and involve the drilling of at least one or two exploratory wells at an estimated cost of $12 million.

The Indian firm said it was the first oil and gas venture by an Indian firm in Kazakhstan, whose Pavlador basin has "promising structures for further exploration" and is the southward extension of the oil-rich west Siberian basin.

ONGC Videsh submitted an application for allotment of an exploration acreage in the Pavlador basin in January, and the Kazakh prime minister signed the award of the exploration licence on May 12, it said.
